correctness.rationale: Exact rational first-difference reduction gives an induced l1 column norm; all diagonal signs are controlled since alpha u_j v_j<1. The sharp step input saturates each column, the M=0 threshold follows at p=2, and Stirling yields M_p/binom(2p,p)->sqrt2. An independent Fraction-based direct matrix inversion checked p=1..12 for three positive rational lambda values. Limits in p are analytic, not inferred from finite numerics.

value.rationale: The exact sharp variation amplification quantifies worst-case creation of adjacent variation by a standard penalized smoothing method. It identifies three distinct low-order regimes, proves that monotone one-step data can be worst cases, and shows a universal high-order amplification of 1+sqrt2 despite arbitrarily small fixed positive penalty. A natural complete classification of the minimal admissible observation length with a nontrivial binomial asymptotic is useful in stability and trend-filter interpretation.
